# Retrospective: PR #12867

## Worked

Fresh Claude Code Opus 5 xhigh and Pi Astra xhigh sessions received equivalent neutral scope. Native identities and effort were verified. No quota exhaustion was claimed. Both independently investigated source and ran isolated tests/rendering. Saved images made the one-property visual change easy to adjudicate. A passing baseline-negative-control and actual mutation outputs supported a proportionate optional test note.

## Errors, evidence and remediation

- Coordinator initially used a broad Claude argv listing, incidentally exposing other agents' launch arguments. No reports or conclusions were read. Switched to owned-pane process-info; future identity discovery must use that endpoint only. Transcript retains the error.
- Opus ran some version/capability/syntax probes on the host despite the assignment. Host results are not evidence for the public claims. Canonical sandboxed prerequisites and independent Astra evidence replace them. No CLI version exception is necessary for native reviewer identity: owned argv/native events suffice.
- Opus listed the peer directory's filenames/sizes but read no peer files. The assignment now explicitly prohibits sibling enumeration as well as peer-report reading. Independent conclusions remain uncontaminated.
- Opus's first fixture used a failing local-variable expansion inside command substitution, then continued scoring later cases. Entire initial node bundle is invalid and retained. Corrected runs validate case tree identity and preserve real prerequisite/case exits. Builder failures need explicit caller-side handling, not reliance on subshell exit. Never count later assertions after setup failure.
- A diagnostic mount display selected the inherited read-only /tmp entry rather than its effective private writable tmpfs. Full mount data and actual private paths establish containment; the incorrect display is not used as safety evidence.
- Astra's first two render attempts failed on a diagnostic alias conflicting with a final QQuickItem property. Both failed immediately and preserved raw logs. Corrected v3 renamed aliases and repeated all cases. These are fixture errors, not product defects or isolation failures.

The responsible Opus assignment has an appended remediation section and a coordinator follow-up asks for explicit acknowledgement. All failed/invalid artifacts remain preserved. No process deviation is concealed by the technically publishable outcome. `safety_process_compliant` is false in the completion package; required technical/editorial gates are assessed separately.

## Carry forward

Use named, non-conflicting observation IDs, console logs from process start, explicit setup prerequisites, and actual child/producer outcomes. Resolve mutation targets before creation/copy/chmod, including helper operations. Keep every runtime probe inside review.py, even quick fixture syntax checks. Use owned pane identity APIs, not user-wide process discovery. Keep synthetic render geometry and fonts visible in reports; do not extrapolate one narrow-card screenshot into a general production severity claim.

No confirmed Omadev bug or desktop issue was found because no desktop slot was used. No package/service/configuration changes were needed. Reviewer native sessions, pinned worktrees and sealed evidence are preserved; temporary sandbox homes/processes ended with their owned runs.

## Final remediation acknowledgement
Read reviewers/opus/remediation.md in full. It identifies a further assertion-order deviation: per-case mkdir preceded its containment check in all node fixture versions. Top-level root checks, fixed names and inspected artifact paths show no actual escape, so technical results remain usable; the ordering is not described as compliant. Future assignments require target resolution before each mutation and caller-side builder failure checks. Opus withdraws the CLI-version exception and confirms all nine owned sandboxes completed and no resources remain.

**Verified:** At `4472ae8b`, the reminder typing line retains the newly typed end of long messages. No important production defect was found in the reviewed scope. The added assertions pass on head and reject the pre-fix QML.

Isolated Qt rendering of the production `Text` block, in a synthetic fixed-width scene:

| Input | Baseline: `ElideRight` | PR: `ElideLeft` |
|---|---|---|
| Long message ending `before lunch` | Ending hidden | Ending visible |
| Appended `TOMORROW` | Appended word hidden | Appended word visible |
| Short message or `15` minutes | Complete text visible | Complete text visible |

Source inspection confirms that submission still uses the full `filterText`, not the elided display.

**Optional test improvement:** Scope the two new assertions in `test/shell.d/reminders-test.sh` to the typing-line `Text` block. In diagnostic copies, changing that line to `ElideMiddle` and adding an unrelated `ElideLeft` label still passed; adding an unrelated `ElideRight` label failed despite the typing line remaining correct. Block-scoped assertions distinguished both cases. This is test-only coverage feedback, not a defect in the current typing behavior.

## Review information

**Test scope:** Targeted reminder tests, baseline negative control, diagnostic mutations and offscreen Qt 6.11.2 rendering of single-line, left-to-right text. No full reminder dialog, real keyboard/IME interaction, RTL coverage, end-to-end reminder creation or full test-suite run. Rendered font and geometry were synthetic, not a theme matrix.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra initial source inspection, independent Opus 5 xhigh and Astra xhigh technical reviews, followed by Astra synthesis and verification against saved targeted evidence. A fresh Astra Medium session checked presentation and compliance only.
